newsitem.title: USA: NYC, Mt. Sinai hospital reach new pact - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYC, Mt. Sinai hospital reach new pact - paper.

text.p: New York City and Mount Sinai Medical Center reached a pact under which the city will pay the center $94 million to run two city hospitals in fiscal 1998, the New York Times said on Wednesday.

The medical center last week spurned an agreement with the city that would have paid it $6 million more to run the Queens and Elmhurst Hospital Centers, in a dispute over how much control the city could exert.

The paper said the deal was a major victory for the Giuliani Administration and the hospital corporation, which has been seeking more control over its 11 public hospitals, demanding more oversight and accountability from its partners.
Under the new agreement, the hospital corporation can appoint and remove medical directors of the two hospitals, and Mount Sinai must meet performance standards or pay financial penalities.

The value of the hospital's contract would fall to $91.7 million in 1999 and might decline another $20 million if the city decides to add some technical workers from Mount Sinai to its own payroll, the paper said.
